solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former or old
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the possessive S

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word error

explanation.surface: A plea to pardon a veteran policeman for a mistake at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgive a fault is to pardon it, a straight verb synonym.

parts.note: the head of the word egg, its first letter, is E
a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: Supplying an intellectual with a clever one-liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual, but it means the head (first letter) of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to furnish or supply them with what they need, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Desert traveller books into legendary English town

parts.note: a camel is the classic beast that crosses deserts
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A camel finds its way into a storied English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is King Arthur's court in Arthurian legend, a mythical English place.

clue.text: Self-conscious when finding condom in the undergrowth

indicators.note: the clue has the protective item placed in the bashful word, which wraps round it

parts.note: shy means self-conscious or bashful
rubber is slang for a condom

explanation.surface: An embarrassed person stumbles on a used contraceptive among the bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container: the bashful word wraps round the slang word for a condom, which is British slang there.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is an area of bushes, close in sense to undergrowth or low dense planting.

clue.text: Union leader is more confident having taken much interest

definitions.note: a phrase describing a person who charges heavy interest on loans; the answer is that person

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here taken from Union

parts.note: surer is the comparative of sure, meaning more confident

explanation.surface: A trade union boss grows bolder after showing keen interest in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks like curiosity but means interest charged on loans; the definition is a descriptive phrase for the lender.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer is a moneylender who charges excessive rates on loans.

indicators.note: about here means the word for offspring goes around the power letter

parts.note: issue means offspring, as does seed in the biblical sense
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A question concerning how potent some narcotic is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a matter for discussion but means offspring (SEED), which goes round P.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed is street slang for amphetamine, a stimulant narcotic.

clue.text: Sally makes love with good man in suitable surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says the word for suitable wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: ripe means ready or fit, as in the time is ripe
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
ST, for saint, is the usual crossword good man

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally romances a virtuous man in a fitting setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name but is a witty retort.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty remark, the same as a riposte or comeback.

indicators.note: in places the pamphlet word inside the plant word

parts.note: a rush is a marsh plant, also called a reed
a tract is a short pamphlet or leaflet

explanation.surface: A flyer was hastily called off in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like haste but is the marsh plant; 'in' puts the pamphlet word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Retracted means withdrawn or taken back, much like a cancelled statement.

parts.note: to sum is to add up
Mary is a girl's name; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone appends something to a young woman's CV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Résumé' looks like a CV but means a summing-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A résumé in its original sense is a brief recap of the main points.

clue.text: Undeterred by discharge in the river

indicators.note: in says the discharge word sits within the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales/England
to spit is to discharge from the mouth

explanation.surface: Pollution is being pumped into a river regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the river' is a British river commonly used in crosswords; 'in' puts the discharge word inside its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Despite means notwithstanding, in spite of, unhindered by something.

clue.text: Warder has studio constructed in jail

indicators.note: in puts the rebuilt letters inside the prison word

parts.note: the can is slang for prison

indicators.note: constructed tells us the letters of studio are built into a new order

explanation.surface: A prison guard has a studio built inside the jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructed' rearranges the six letters to give USTODI; 'in' places that inside the American slang word for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A warder is a keeper or guardian, so a custodian in charge of something.

indicators.note: after puts the leaping word following the period word

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
to bound is to leap or skip

explanation.surface: Carried off, a child skips along after a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' looks like being moved, but means enraptured.
explanation.definitionFit: To be transported is to be carried away with delight, i.e. enchanted or entranced.

parts.note: a wag is a joker or comic

explanation.surface: Another comic is said to be very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' here means stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is loot, stolen goods, which are hot in thieves' slang.

clue.text: Hit man is to have a swim

parts.note: to bat is to strike, as with a bat
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A contract killer plans to take a dip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit man' looks like an assassin but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe can mean to go swimming, especially in the sea, in British usage.

indicators.note: to become says these two words must turn into something new, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coach someone called Bill until he shines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a verb meaning coach but is anagram fodder with BILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant means shining with great light, very bright and dazzling.

indicators.note: in puts the people word inside the legal wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are people

explanation.surface: Bullying of people goes on in a corrupt society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong society' looks like a phrase but is two pieces: TORT and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Torments as a verb means pesters or harasses, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Blow for Tory given Home Office approval

parts.note: the Tories are the political right in Britain
HO is the abbreviation for Home Office, a UK government department
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: A Conservative gets the Home Office's go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Office is the UK ministry for policing and immigration.
explanation.definitionFit: A right hook is a punch thrown with the right hand, so a blow in boxing.

clue.text: Son might have broken down without being in fear

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside places the outer word around the others

parts.note: a machine that has died has broken down
may expresses possibility, like might

explanation.surface: A son may have collapsed out of sheer fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so DIED surrounds S and MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismayed means filled with alarm or distress, close to being afraid.

parts.note: mad means crazy
on can mean over, resting upon

explanation.surface: Wild enthusiasm over an American idol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Icon' fits both the pop star and a religious image of the Virgin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Madonna is an image of the Virgin Mary, a classic religious icon; also a pop icon.

parts.note: a reed is a woodwind instrument, or a pipe made of reed

explanation.surface: Wanting to possess a fine musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is an excessive desire or craving, a strong form of longing.

clue.text: Nobleman — that is, a king in past times

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A lord, namely a monarch, from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a previous time, so before now, in former times.

parts.note: the PLO is the Palestine Liberation Organization

explanation.surface: Freedom fighters kept going even as one fell.
explanation.definitionFit: To plod is to keep going laboriously, persevering just as soldiering on implies.

clue.text: Carol accepts the problem, having superficial knowledge

indicators.note: accepts says the singing word takes the problem word into itself

parts.note: to carol is to sing
what's the matter? asks what the problem is

explanation.surface: A singer of carols acknowledges the difficulty with only a little learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a name or a song but is the verb SING.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a slight, shallow acquaintance with a subject.

parts.note: a hen that broods sits, so sat
YR is the abbreviation for year, a long time

explanation.surface: A rake sulked for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brooded' suggests moping but means sat on eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a lustful man, after the lecherous woodland gods of myth.

clue.text: Clothes of many Londoners contain this

definitions.text: Clothes of many Londoners contain this

indicators.note: contain says the letters sit inside the words many Londoners

explanation.surface: A remark that city dwellers' garments include some material.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'maNY LONdoners'; the whole clue also defines the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fibre common in everyday garments.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters of gateman are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doorman annoyed a business mogul.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnate is a wealthy, powerful businessperson, the same as a tycoon.

clue.text: Wild beast is all Igor dealt with

indicators.note: dealt with, like cards dealt out, shows the letters of all Igor are redistributed

explanation.surface: A savage animal was handled entirely by Igor.
explanation.walkthrough: Igor evokes Frankenstein's assistant, adding to the monster picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla is a great ape, a large wild animal.

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of nature are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: Something peculiar about a beverage machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea urn is a large metal container with a tap that serves hot tea.

clue.text: Star drinking alcohol is on the slippery slope

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the star word swallows the drink

parts.note: the sun is a star
kir is a drink of white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: A celebrity who drinks is heading for a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a celebrity but is the SUN; 'slippery slope' sounds like moral decline but is a literal snowy piste.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski run is a snow-covered descent, literally an icy, slippery incline.
